BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).

- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

Prepared for the Wattlebridge Holdings deal team. The Seller's documents have been treated as the counterparty's draft and tested against the Buyer Playbook. Note at the outset: the Seller's Disclosure Letter is, in several places, more candid than the Seller's Update – the letter concedes that Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, Ironquay payment proof and bonus funding are all *absent* from the record, which undercuts the "fair and balanced package" characterisation.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation: REJECT; counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** 20% is our conditional fallback only, and no written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft has been given – the Seller's figure cannot be accepted as a starting point.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only (deductible) recovery (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer wants:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar (tipping) recovery once exceeded.
- **Recommendation: REJECT all three elements.** The Seller's thresholds are 5x our positions and the deductible structure permanently forfeits the first AUD 250,000 of loss.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months (cl 12.3/13), plus a default that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly excluded.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months; limitations confined to general Warranty Claims only.
- **Recommendation: REJECT; counter at 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.** 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval (none given), and the catch-all default would pull Title, Tax, IP and indemnity claims into the short limit.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** separate regime – 100% of price cap, at least six years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation: REJECT outright.** Title and capacity go to whether we receive the asset at all; "administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap recovery of AUD 24m at AUD 4.8m with an 18-month fuse.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature"; no fraud carve-out appears anywhere.
- **Buyer wants:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of every cap, basket, time limit, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clause to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation: REJECT; insert an express, non-waivable carve-out.** The omission is a red flag in itself – no one on our side has authority to accept a regime that limits recovery for the Seller's own fraud.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012 as at 22 Sept 2026), Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable records (Sch 7; DL 1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** specific, fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation: REJECT; replace with a "fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope" standard, referenced to specific DL paragraphs.** Whole-data-room disclosure effectively converts every warranty into a representation of what we already found.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** no claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** delete the blanket exclusion; any residual qualifier limited to actual knowledge of named buyer individuals, with no application to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation: DELETE cl 8.3.** "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard that, combined with SPA-N-006, would leave almost no actionable warranty claim.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** reasonable endeavours only; condition deemed satisfied on delivery of written consent (cl 3/6.3). DL §2 admits no final consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are met.
- **Buyer wants:** effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) consent as a Completion condition, with evidence of satisfaction of cl 11.3 conditions delivered before Completion.
- **Recommendation: REJECT.** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue; a consent-on-delivery mechanic lets the Seller complete on a conditional consent whose conditions may never be met.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7). DL §3 confirms no repayment and no final discharge in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation: REJECT.** A debt-free/cash-free deal cannot complete with AUD 3.2m of secured debt and live change-of-control (cl 8.1) outstanding; a post-completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable bank undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval, neither of which exists.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** DD-005 AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. DL §5 confirms omission and is silent on payroll tax/super/on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** the AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item funded by the Seller (or deducted from price as a Debt/transaction cost).
- **Recommendation: REJECT; require express treatment.** "A matter for the Seller" with no mechanism means the Company (i.e. the Buyer post-Completion) pays – the funds flow must not silently exclude it.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** indemnity confined to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). DL §4 concedes no receipt, no confirmatory assignment, and that the AUD 180,000 in DD-010 is not independently verified.
- **Buyer wants:** broadened indemnity covering title/ownership defects in SOW3 Project Materials, third-party claims and costs of perfecting title, while preserving the cl 7.3 cure (payment triggers transfer).
- **Recommendation: REJECT as drafted; broaden and require pre-Completion cure or escrow.** Until every SOW3 fee is cleared the Company does not own the deliverables, and an indemnity limited to one invoice does not cover the ownership consequences; treat the AUD 180,000 as unverified in both directions.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sch 6). DL §6 confirms ~1,240 records, unknown access, unknown scope, notification not yet determined.
- **Buyer wants:** log preservation, a completed investigation, pre-Completion updates and a specific indemnity for notification/remediation costs if a breach is confirmed.
- **Recommendation: DO NOT ACCEPT the "not material" characterisation; require investigation undertakings and a specific indemnity, without asserting a breach.** The record establishes neither breach nor harm nor a notification duty, so the right posture is to preserve evidence and shift risk, not to price a number into the deal.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** three AUD 110,000 renewals (AUD 330,000) are ordinary-course operating costs. DL §8 is silent on whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** an assessment of timing, termination rights and accrual before accepting the characterisation; no automatic Debt treatment or price deduction.
- **Recommendation: ASSESS; reserve position.** Reading DD-008 and DD-011 together is required before deciding whether any component is a Debt-like or leakage item – neither acceptance nor deduction is warranted on the current record.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13), plus cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 covering "all Claims of any nature"; Tax and IP "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment (purchase price/completion) and covenant claims each with their own regime and no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation: REJECT; redraft so that the general regime applies only to defined General Warranty Claims.** The Seller has used three separate clauses to achieve a single result – collapsing every category into the 20%/18-month/AUD 250,000 box – and each must be reversed.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** title to 100% of shares evidenced by the DD-012 share register. DL §10 concedes DD-012 is simply "the source relied on" and that no Buyer verification is stated.
- **Buyer wants:** independent evidence – ASIC extracts, constitution, share certificates, board/member approvals, PPSR and encumbrance searches, and authority/capacity confirmation for Harbourglass.
- **Recommendation: DO NOT RELY on DD-012 alone; commission independent searches and make clean title a Completion deliverable.** An internal register is the Seller's own document, not third-party proof, and the Riverlark security (SPA-N-009) makes an encumbrance search essential.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** separate tax (and tax indemnity) and IP warranty regimes with their own caps and periods; terms remain OPEN.
- **Recommendation: REJECT the "settled" characterisation; record both as open.** Nothing has been agreed; our position assumes neither unlimited Seller liability nor resolution, and the Seller's attempt to fold these into cl 12 is simply SPA-N-014 by another route.

---

### Summary of priority points for the mark-up
1. **Deal-structural (must fix before Completion):** Bluefen consent (N-008), Riverlark payout/release (N-009), independent title evidence (N-015).
2. **Liability architecture (reject as a package):** cap (N-001), thresholds (N-002), time limit (N-003), fundamental regime (N-004), fraud carve-out (N-005), category separation (N-014), Tax/IP (N-016).
3. **Disclosure/knowledge (delete):** N-006, N-007.
4. **Specific risk allocation (require express mechanisms):** bonuses (N-010), Ironquay (N-011), DD-006 incident (N-012).
5. **Assess further:** Sandbar (N-013).

No fallback position in the Playbook has been triggered; each requires prior written approval from Amelia Frost identifying the specific draft, and none has been given.
